## Summary

The `reconcile-check` vocabulary was retired by `mechanical-bitter-basenji`
(`0cfc-e511-8f8a-4c8b`, merged as `8e14d667da28`), but one **live state path** still writes it.
This is a deliberate, operator-directed carve-out from that story — filed here so it is tracked
debt rather than an unexplained residual.

## The residual

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py`

- **`:717`** — the pause **writer** still persists `gated_mode="reconcile-check"`.
- **`:658`** — the matching **decoder**.

Everything else in the retired family is clean. A whole-tree sweep
(`grep -rn "reconcile-check\|reconcile_check\|RECONCILE_CHECK"`) at `12a10f3ab4ef` found
`.github/`, `Jenkinsfile`, `scripts/` and `src/rebar/schemas/` free of it, and the remaining hits
are all explained:

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mode.py:57` — the **intentional** narrow decode alias
  retained by 0cfc's AC3: it maps only the persisted sentinel to `DRY_RUN`, is not an enum member,
  and is absent from `MODE_CAPS`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/request.py:102-104` — the retirement **rejection message**,
  which must name the retired vocabulary in order to route users to `preview` / `fsck` / `status`.
- `docs/adr/0092`, `docs/adr/0099`, `docs/adr/0083` — ADR prose. Historical records of decisions
  taken when the vocabulary was live; rewriting them would falsify the record.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py:350` — the `"reconcile_check_error"` log key. **Unrelated
  subsystem** (the review-bot's Gerrit vote-reconcile loop). A name collision, not a residual.
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/...` — frozen eval fixtures and corpora.

So `_ref_lock.py:658/717` is the only genuine live-state survivor.

## Why it was left

0cfc's description carries a "Final AC2 Option B execution note" recording that **the operator
explicitly directed that pass not to edit** the pause-state decoder/writer at those lines. That is
a description-level carve-out, not a comment-level one, so it was a deliberate scope decision
rather than an omission. It does mean 0cfc's AC2 ("no live route/mode/state path retains the
vocabulary") cannot be satisfied on a literal reading, which is why that ticket's AC2 now points
here.

## Why it is low priority but not zero

The value is persisted pause state, and the decoder that reads it is present and correct, so
nothing is broken today. The cost is that a retired name survives in written state: any future
reader of a pause record sees vocabulary the codebase otherwise says does not exist, and a later
cleanup that removes the decoder without migrating the writer would strand existing pause records.
The two lines must therefore move together.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 The pause **writer** at `_ref_lock.py:717` persists a current-vocabulary value instead of
      `"reconcile-check"`.
- [ ] AC2 Existing persisted pause records written with the old sentinel are **still readable** —
      either migrated, or read by a narrowly-retained decoder in the same shape as the one AC3 of
      0cfc already sanctions in `mode.py:57`. Dropping the decoder in the same change that changes
      the writer is the failure mode this AC exists to prevent.
- [ ] AC3 A test writes a pause record with the OLD sentinel and asserts it still decodes correctly
      after the change, and a second test asserts new writes use the new value. Both directions, so
      the migration cannot silently break old records.
- [ ] AC4 The whole-tree sweep for `reconcile-check|reconcile_check|RECONCILE_CHECK` is re-run and
      its output recorded here, with every surviving hit individually explained (the categories
      above are the expected survivors: the intentional decode alias, the rejection message, ADR
      prose, the unrelated review-bot log key, and frozen eval fixtures).
- [ ] AC5 `0cfc-e511-8f8a-4c8b`'s AC2 disposition is updated to note the residual is discharged.

## Constraints

Never use `--force` or any gate bypass. `timeout` does not exist on this macOS host (it exits 127,
a silent no-op) — bound with `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'`. Do not touch the shared main
checkout; do not `git stash` anywhere.
